gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a power station left with its AC inverter on in an empty shed burns about 15 W around the clock. Hobotech measured 88 Wh in 6 h on the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, which works out to about 352 Wh a day. That is about 94% of one 200 W panel's northern-winter harvest (200 W × 2.5 h × 0.75 = 375 Wh), so a winter shed needs the 2 × 200 W panels (750 Wh) or the AC switched off or put in ECO mode between uses.
standout_why: I read ecosolarkits.com (cited in both chats) and wattfolk.com (cited in chat 2) on 2026-11-10. Both give daily-Wh, panel and battery formulas and the warning that LiFePO4 can't charge below freezing. Neither gives an inverter idle or standby draw, a self-discharge figure, or any line that adds the station's own consumption to the daily load. I couldn't open agripure.org (cited in chat 1) or solargenadvisor.com (top result in chat 1) because of a self-signed-certificate error, so I can't rule out that they cover it. If they don't, this finding decides the set: one 200 W panel versus two, or a must-do setting. That would make it a 3.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4, 2,600 W AC). StorageReview measured 1.91 kWh delivered, enough for ecosolarkits' 1,020 Wh/day hobby-workshop example with one day spare. 2,600 W continuous covers that page's 1,900 W saw-plus-lights inverter target.

Solar panels: 2 × BLUETTI 200 W SP200L (400 W), not 1 × 200 W. In winter, 400 W × 2.5 h × 0.75 = 750 Wh/day, which covers the 352 Wh/day AC idle draw plus about 400 Wh of real load. One panel (375 Wh) is used up by idle alone. 400 W is well under the station's 1,000 W / 12–60 V / 20 A solar input.

Setting, not a product: switch AC off when you leave the shed, or turn on the Elite 200 V2's ECO mode or Auto Sleep (StorageReview names both). With only DC on, Hobotech measured 144 Wh/day instead of 352 Wh/day.
Solar cable (MC4 to the station's input): BLUETTI's Australian Elite 200 V2 page says the station doesn't include one. I couldn't confirm whether the US 2 × 200 W bundle includes it.

findings.label: No-load draw with the AC inverter on (measured)
findings.value: about 15 W (88 Wh in 6 h; about 352 Wh per 24 h)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 v2 — crazy efficient 2600W portable solar power station (HOBOTECH Tom, 2024-11-13)
findings.note: Phantom-load test, AC on, nothing plugged in. 88 Wh ÷ 6 h = 14.7 W; × 24 h = 352 Wh/day. Hobotech calls it 'a very exceptional 15w at idle for a 2600w inverter'.

findings.label: No-load draw with only the DC outputs on (measured)
findings.value: about 6 W (72 Wh in 12 h; about 144 Wh per 24 h)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 v2 — crazy efficient 2600W portable solar power station (HOBOTECH Tom)
findings.note: 72 Wh ÷ 12 h = 6 W. Running 12 V lights from DC with the AC off saves about 208 Wh/day against AC idle (352 − 144).

findings.label: Winter harvest of one 200 W panel compared with the station's AC idle draw
findings.source_title: How Much Solar Power Does a Shed Need? Kit Sizing (2026) | Eco Solar Kits
findings.note: Eco Solar Kits' formula: panel W × peak sun h × 0.75, with northern winter at 2–3.5 sun h. Using 2.5 h: 200 × 2.5 × 0.75 = 375 Wh, and 352 ÷ 375 = 94%. With 2 × 200 W: 750 Wh, so idle takes 47% and about 398 Wh is left for loads.

findings.label: Rival's daily-load example (hobby workshop)
findings.value: 1,020 Wh/day; 400 W of panels and 1.1 kWh minimum battery
findings.source_title: How Much Solar Power Does a Shed Need? Kit Sizing (2026) | Eco Solar Kits
findings.note: 4 LED × 15 W × 4 h + saw 1,400 W × 0.25 h + charger 100 W × 2 h + radio 20 W × 4 h + fan 50 W × 3 h. If the AC is left on 24 h, the true daily need is 1,020 − (idle already in the load hours, about 15 W × 4 h = 60) + 352 ≈ 1,312 Wh. The page doesn't account for this.

findings.label: Measured energy delivered from full
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review (Dylan Dougherty, StorageReview, 2025-04-25)
findings.note: Discharge test. 1.91 ÷ 2.0736 = 92% of rated. AC idle alone empties a full battery in 1,910 ÷ 352 ≈ 5.4 sunless days. Hobotech's AC capacity test gave 1,990 Wh.

findings.label: Rated capacity and AC output
findings.value: 2,073.6 Wh; 2,600 W continuous (3,900 W Power Lifting, resistive loads only)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2+2*200W Solar (BLUETTI US store)
findings.note: From the maker's US page. 2,600 W covers Eco Solar Kits' 1,900 W target for a 1,400 W saw plus 160 W of lights.
